notes: Isolates simultaneous negative constraints over a closed vocabulary: no E-bearing word, no repeated word, exactly one Z-bearing word per line, plus positive slots (TOPAZ/QUILL/MAROON) and a per-line first/last-initial rule. Confound removed: the vocabulary closes the output space, so gibberish and off-list words cannot pass, and no content judgement is involved. Tier 3: 38 of the 58 entries are E-free and exactly four E-free entries contain Z, so rule 5 forces those four one-per-line - a planner that picks words greedily tends to strand a Z-word; strong-model prior 40-70%. Grading is rule-checking, not equality with one witness, so any valid inscription passes and the verdict stays deterministic. False-positive audit: (a) an E-bearing entry used, (b) two Z-words on one line, (c) a repeated word, (d) a 6-word line, (e) an off-vocabulary gibberish word, (f) numbered lines, (g) missing TOPAZ - all rejected.
contamination_source: original (constrained-writing exercise; vocabulary and rule set are bespoke)
